<title>Marrowbeck Ferries: radio interview on the October cancellations</title>
<transcript>
[0] Calum Reddy: This is the Friday transport hour.
[1] Calum Reddy: With me are Ione Farraday, operations manager at Marrowbeck Ferries, and Bram Oxley, the harbour master at Marrowbeck.
[2] Calum Reddy: Thank you both.
[3] Ione Farraday: Good to be here.
[4] Bram Oxley: Morning.
[5] Calum Reddy: Ione, start with the basics.
[6] Calum Reddy: What does the service normally run?
[7] Ione Farraday: Six sailings a day between Marrowbeck and Tarn Island, with two vessels, the Skerry Lass and the Eilean.
[8] Calum Reddy: And October was a bad month.
[9] Ione Farraday: It was.
[10] Ione Farraday: We cancelled 14 sailings in October.
[11] Calum Reddy: Why?
[12] Ione Farraday: Weather.
[13] Ione Farraday: We had gusts over 40 knots on several days, and we do not sail in that.
[14] Bram Oxley: I have to disagree with that.
[15] Bram Oxley: My log shows weather closed the harbour on two days.
[16] Bram Oxley: That accounts for 5 of the 14 sailings.
[17] Calum Reddy: And the other 9?
[18] Bram Oxley: The other 9 were cancelled on days when the harbour was open and other boats were moving.
[19] Bram Oxley: My understanding is the Eilean had no master.
[20] Ione Farraday: The Eilean's master was off sick for part of the month, that is true.
[21] Calum Reddy: So was it weather or was it crew?
[22] Ione Farraday: I would still say weather was the main cause.
[23] Ione Farraday: Conditions outside the harbour can be worse than inside it.
[24] Bram Oxley: I would say crew was the main cause.
[25] Bram Oxley: Nine is more than five.
[26] Calum Reddy: You are not going to agree on that.
[27] Ione Farraday: Probably not today.
[28] Calum Reddy: What happened to the passengers?
[29] Ione Farraday: We refunded 312 passengers in October.
[30] Ione Farraday: Everyone who asked got their money back within a week.
[31] Calum Reddy: Is the crew problem fixed?
[32] Ione Farraday: We have hired a second master for the Eilean.
[33] Ione Farraday: She starts on the first of December.
[34] Bram Oxley: That will help.
[35] Bram Oxley: A boat with one master is one cold away from staying tied up.
[36] Calum Reddy: Bram, anything the harbour is changing?
[37] Bram Oxley: We are putting a wind gauge on the outer wall, so that both of us are reading the same number.
[38] Bram Oxley: It goes in next month.
[39] Ione Farraday: I welcome that.
[40] Ione Farraday: It would have saved us this argument.
[41] Calum Reddy: Ione Farraday, Bram Oxley, thank you.
</transcript>

points.text: Marrowbeck Ferries normally runs six sailings a day between Marrowbeck and Tarn Island with two vessels, the Skerry Lass and the Eilean.
Marrowbeck Ferries cancelled 14 sailings in October.
Ione Farraday attributes the cancellations mainly to weather, citing gusts over 40 knots on several days and saying conditions outside the harbour can be worse than inside.
Harbour master Bram Oxley says his log shows weather closed the harbour on two days, accounting for 5 of the 14 cancelled sailings.
Oxley says the other 9 cancellations happened on days when the harbour was open and other boats were moving, and that the Eilean had no master.
Farraday confirms the Eilean's master was off sick for part of the month.
Oxley considers crew the main cause because 9 is more than 5.
The ferry company refunded 312 passengers in October, and says everyone who asked got their money back within a week.
A second master has been hired for the Eilean and starts on 1 December.
Oxley says a boat with one master is one cold away from staying tied up.
The harbour will install a wind gauge on the outer wall next month so both parties read the same number; Farraday welcomes it.
